# Framework mapping

<!-- Generated by `tracestate frameworks --format markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every control TraceState's rules evidence, and the rules that test it. Generated from 35 rules (builtin:default_rules.yaml).

A mapping means a violation of the rule is evidence *against* the control. A clean scan shows the specific checks passed; it does not certify the control, which also covers process, people and infrastructure that no code scanner can see.

## CIS Docker Benchmark (recommendation titles)

| Control | Title | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `bind-host-interface` | Published ports are bound to a specific host interface | TS-CTR-008 |
| `no-docker-socket` | The Docker socket is not mounted inside containers | TS-CTR-003 |
| `no-host-namespaces` | Host network, PID and IPC namespaces are not shared | TS-CTR-004 |
| `no-privileged` | Privileged containers are not used | TS-CTR-002 |
| `no-secrets-in-env` | Secrets are not stored in container environment or image layers | TS-CTR-006, TS-IMG-004 |
| `non-root-user` | Containers run as a non-root user | TS-CTR-001, TS-IMG-001 |
| `pinned-images` | Images are pinned to an immutable version | TS-CTR-005, TS-IMG-002 |
| `trusted-build-inputs` | Build inputs come from trusted, verified sources | TS-IMG-003 |
